text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD

- Finance Minister Rudolf Edlinger expects to save one billion schillings for the budget through plans to cut premiums on building society contracts. Up to 1,500 jobs in the building industry are jeoparized by the plans.

- Defence Minister Werner Fasslabend wants Austria's army to comply with NATO standards in preparation for possible membership in the military alliance. Social Democrat chief whip Peter Kostelka has strongly criticized the move as a breach of the constitution.
- Austrian Airlines will be privatised next year, as the government plans to participate in the company's capital increase and will thereby lose its majority.
- Austria's inflation rose slightly to 1.7 percent in May from 1.5 percent the month before.
- Italian Gildemeister is expected to take over machinery producer Emco, after Emco's creditor banks refused the offer of the company's former owners to take it over.
- Milk producers Berglandmilch and Obersteirische Molkerei will build a joint logistics centre and dairy in north-west Styria.
- Foodstuffs group Mautner-Markhof's agreement with Germany's Eckes to licence the company's drinks unit, has now been passed by the shareholders.
DIE PRESSE
- Conservative Karl Jellasitz is against his People's Party's plan to buy new aeroplanes for Austria's army.
- Trade unions are up in arms over the government's plan to reform the public pension system.
- Austria's hi-tech companies plan to participate in the European Space Agency's commercial projects which are expected to reach a turnover of 20 billion ECU.
KURIER
- Social Democrats are demanding the resignation of conservative Defence Minister Fasslabend as the coalition split widens over Austria's future security policies.
- Austria's membership of the European Union's Schengen agreement will be delayed as the French parliament can only ratify it this autumn.

- Creditanstalt head Gerhard Novy expects a bigger group of countries to be members in the European Economic and Monetary Union, saying this would not undermine the strength of the single currency euro.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- New car production facilities by Opel/General Motors, Isuzu and Daewoo in Poland bring new hope to Austria's car supply producers.
- Economic research institute Wifo expert Thomas Url says company pension schemes could make cuts in the public pensions system more bearable.
